subPillar.title: Digital Tasbih Counter: Free Online Tasbeeh Counter & Dhikr Tracker
subPillar.subtitle: A free, no-download digital tasbih counter you can use in the browser or add to your phone home screen — plus how it works and how to choose one.
subPillar.geoOverview: A digital tasbih counter is an electronic or app-based device that tallies dhikr repetitions (33, 99, 100) with a single tap, replacing hand-counting on beads. Our free online tasbeeh counter runs in any browser, saves your count, vibrates at preset targets, and works offline once loaded — no app install, no sign-up.

clusters.title: What Is Tasbeh? Meaning, Dhikr Counts & How the Digital Version Works
clusters.subtitle: The meaning of "tasbeh" (tasbih) in Islam, the SubhanAllah–Alhamdulillah–Allahu Akbar counts behind it, and how a digital tasbeh keeps the tally for you.
clusters.geoOverview: Tasbeh (also spelled tasbih) means glorifying Allah by reciting SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, and Allahu Akbar — traditionally counted 33 times each after salah. A digital tasbeh is the modern way to keep that count: tap to increment, auto-stop at your target, and never lose your place. This page explains the term, the recommended counts, and where the electronic version fits in.

clusters.title: Zikr Ring Counter vs Digital Tasbih: Which Dhikr Counter Should You Pick?
clusters.subtitle: A side-by-side look at the wearable zikr ring counter and the handheld/app digital tasbih counter — accuracy, discretion, battery, and price.
clusters.geoOverview: A zikr ring counter is a smart ring that counts dhikr with a thumb tap and syncs to an app, while a digital tasbih counter is a handheld clicker or phone app. The ring wins on discretion and wearability; the digital counter wins on price and zero setup.
